documents.title: SCIT Annual Review
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
MILL RIVER ENT & ALLERGY
Allergen immunotherapy, yearly review

Tyler Boucher. Subcutaneous grass/tree/weed pollen extract, monthly maintenance, continuing. We have reviewed his updated history including the diagnosis of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency he reports from pulmonology last year, with an albuterol inhaler as needed and weekly augmentation infusions at home; no change to his injection plan. No injection reactions. Continue cetirizine and fluticasone nasal as he uses them. Review in 12 months.

Otolaryngology

documents.title: PA Request: Fluticasone Nasal
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Fax from pharmacy: Medicaid rejected fluticasone propionate nasal 16 g, 'quantity exceeds plan limit, PA required'.
Reviewed: sig is 2 sprays each nostril daily = 1 bottle per 30 days, within plan limit. Called pharmacy, claim had been entered as a 15-day supply. Pharmacist corrected to 30 days and claim paid. No PA needed. Pt picked up per pharmacy.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
SUGARLOAF PULMONARY ASSOCIATES
Yearly review, 06/18/2024

Re: Tyler Boucher, DOB 07/29/1991

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Boucher has had weekly augmentation infusions at home since 08/17/2023 without any infusion reaction. He uses the albuterol a few times a month, mostly on longer walks. His breathlessness is unchanged, at about two blocks of walking. No cough, no chest infections. Never smoker. Medications: augmentation weekly, albuterol as needed, cetirizine as needed, fluticasone nasal spray, monthly allergen immunotherapy.

Examination: SpO2 95% on room air at rest. Thin, comfortable. Expiratory phase mildly prolonged, hyperresonant to percussion, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular. No clubbing, cyanosis or edema.

Spirometry today: FEV1/FVC 0.57, unchanged from 06/2023.

Assessment: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, PiZZ, with lower-lobe emphysema, stable on augmentation.

Plan: continue alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor (human) 60 mg/kg IV weekly by home infusion and albuterol HFA 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Review in a year with spirometry.

Pulmonology, Sugarloaf Pulmonary Associates
cc: PCP

documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
KESTREL HILL NEUROLOGY, Neuromuscular Clinic
Yearly review, 08/20/2024

Re: Tyler Boucher, DOB 07/29/1991

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Boucher is stable. Weekly augmentation infusions for his alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency since last August, albuterol as needed. Limb strength and stairs as before, occasional double vision, no trouble swallowing, no palpitations or faints, no hearing change. Still walking most days within his breathing limits.

Examination unchanged: bilateral ptosis, limited eye movements in more than one direction, mild proximal limb weakness.

ECG today: sinus rhythm 60/min, PR 162 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 410 ms. Normal and unchanged.

Plan: continue the home exercise program. Review in a year with an ECG.

Sincerely,
Neurology, Kestrel Hill Neurology
cc: PCP

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT, 33M

First full physical since 2021 (missed 2022, problem visits in 2023).

Interval: Breathing about where it was last summer, winded at a couple of blocks, manages working from home. Weekly augmentation infusions at home since 8/2023, no reactions; albuterol a few times a month. Pulm review 6/18: spirometry unchanged (FEV1/FVC 0.57), continue the same. Neurology review 8/20: exam and ECG unchanged, keeps walking most days. No change in weakness or the ptosis. Still on monthly allergy shots at Mill River, no reactions, using cetirizine and the spray in season. No ED or urgent care visits. No new symptoms.

Problems: allergic rhinitis due to pollen (SCIT since 2020); mitochondrial myopathy (2021) with exercise intolerance; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, PiZZ, with lower-lobe emphysema (2023); transaminases mildly elevated since 2023.
Meds: cetirizine 10 mg PRN, fluticasone nasal 2 sprays each nostril daily, SCIT monthly, albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h PRN, alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor 60 mg/kg IV weekly (home infusion, pulm).
Allergies: tree, grass, weed pollen. NKDA.
FH: reviewed, unchanged from 7/2023.
Social: freelance graphic designer at home. Never smoker. AUDIT-C 2 (1-2 drinks/wk). No drugs.
PHQ-2: 0.

VS: BP 111/69, HR 65, RR 18, T 36.9, SpO2 95% RA, wt 64.9 kg, BMI 20.2.
Gen: thin, no distress.
HEENT: mild turbinate edema. Eyes: mild bilateral ptosis.
Neck: supple.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Lungs: mildly prolonged expiration, no wheeze, no crackles.
Abd: soft, NT, no HSM.
Ext: no edema or clubbing.
Neuro: mild proximal weakness, unchanged.
Skin: no lesions.

A/P:
1. Preventive: flu vaccine today. PCV20 done 2023. Tdap 2018. HIV/HCV screened 2018. COVID per pharmacy this fall. CBC, CMP today.
2. AATD with emphysema: stable symptoms, SpO2 at his recent baseline. Weekly augmentation and PRN albuterol per pulm.
3. Transaminases / mitochondrial myopathy: CMP and CK today. Neurology following yearly.
4. Allergic rhinitis on SCIT.
RTC 1 year, labs again in 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical, 34-year-old man.

Since last year: no new problems. Monthly allergy injections continue at Mill River, no reactions. Breathing unchanged, still a couple of blocks before he has to stop. Weekly augmentation infusions at home continue, albuterol now and then; pulm 6/17: spirometry unchanged. Neurology 8/18: stable, ECG normal. Muscle weakness and the droopy lids about the same. Working freelance design from home, steady. Sleeping fine. Mood good.

Active problems:
- Allergic rhinitis due to pollen, on SCIT
- Mitochondrial myopathy, with exercise intolerance
- Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (PiZZ), lower-lobe emphysema; mild transaminase elevation
Meds: cetirizine 10 mg PRN, fluticasone nasal daily, SCIT monthly (outside), albuterol HFA PRN, alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor 60 mg/kg IV weekly (home infusion, pulm).
Allergies: tree/grass/weed pollen; NKDA.
PHQ-9: 1.
Never smoker; 1-2 drinks/wk.

Vitals: BP 117/68, HR 69, RR 15, T 36.9, SpO2 94% RA, wt 63.2 kg, BMI 19.7.
General: thin, comfortable.
Eyes: mild bilateral ptosis.
ENT: nasal mucosa slightly pale. Oropharynx clear.
Heart: regular, no murmur.
Lungs: mild prolongation of expiration, clear otherwise.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, no clubbing.
Neuro: mild proximal weakness, stable.
Mood/affect: normal.

Assessment and plan:
1. Health maintenance: flu shot given in clinic today. Depression screen negative. Vaccines otherwise current. CBC, CMP, CK drawn.
2. AATD with emphysema: stable on weekly augmentation, PRN albuterol, per pulm.
3. Mitochondrial myopathy: stable, neurology yearly.
4. Allergic rhinitis: continue SCIT and current meds.
Back in 6 months for a check-in and labs.
